summary.name: Incident Management at Netflix Velocity
summary.one_liner: A conference talk page on InfoQ where Netflix Senior SRE Dave Hahn describes how Netflix engineering handles system failures, incidents, and the training behind them.
use_cases: Learning how Netflix thinks about and handles production failures
Understanding chaos engineering as part of reliability practice
Reviewing incident management training and techniques
Preparing for on-call and incident response work
Studying how to avoid blaming human error for complex failures
summary.what_it_does: The page is an InfoQ presentation listing for a QCon talk by Dave Hahn, a Senior SRE in Netflix's Cloud Operations and Reliability Engineering organization. The summary says the talk covers how Netflix engineering teams think about failure and the tools, techniques, and training they use to shorten failures and their impact on customers. It argues that chaos is useful, failure is guaranteed, and Netflix benefits from having both. The page gives no detail on specific tools or procedures beyond this summary. It also has a bio for the speaker and a generic description of the QCon conference.
notable: Speaker is a Senior SRE at Netflix in Cloud Operations and Reliability Engineering
Talk argues that chaos is a friend and failure is guaranteed
Focuses on human error mis-attribution in complex problems
Presented at QCon and hosted on InfoQ
caveats: Page is a talk summary only; no transcript or slides are included in the text
Specific tools and techniques named in the talk are not listed on this page
